text:
We do not know how to say goodbye:

we wander about, shoulder to shoulder.

Already the sun is setting,

you go taciturn, I am your shadow.


Let us go into a church to see

baptisms, weddings, funeral masses.

Why are we different from the rest?

Outside again, each one turns their head.


Or let us sit in the cemetery,

on the trampled snow, sighing for one another.

That rod in your hand is drawing mansions

where we will always be together.




1917

translation.title: We Do Not Know How to Say Goodbye
translation.editorial_note: The translation keeps the lovers' inability to part and the imagined mansions drawn in cemetery snow.
